newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia toughens cable rollout rules.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia toughens cable rollout rules.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston said on Friday that pay television companies would be subject to a tougher code governing the rollout of optic fibre cable above ground from July 1.
Alston told reporters above ground cables would have to be grey rather than black and would not be allowed at major intersections.
The tougher rules would apply largely to Optus Vision, which has been installing optic fibre cables for pay television and for telephones along with power lines in major Australia cities.

The state-owned Telstra Corp, which is installing the cable for its Foxtel joint venture with News Corp Ltd, has installed most of its cable underground, but has recently been installing cables overhead to keep its costs down.
"The code will be tightened in a number of significant respects," Alston said.
"For example, it will be a requirement to use grey instead of black coaxial cable. It will be a requirement to go underground at major intersections," he said.
"The carriers will be required to regard visual impact as a mandatory visual consideration," he said.
"July 1 is essentially the start-up date for full and open competition, including a fundamentally different regime for cables."
Alston also said the operators would need the approval of a local council before it could install overhead cables in its jurisdiction.

He said they would also not be able to install overhead cables where there had previously been no overhead cables and would have to go underground when above-ground power cables in that street went underground.
Residents in some areas in Sydney in particular have complained of visual pollution where Optus Vision have installed their cables along with power poles.
Several councils have taken Optus Vision to court, but the rollout has continued because it is allowed under the current telecommunications regime.
Alston has been lobbied hard by back-benchers in his own conservative Liberal party who wanted the roll-out restricted or stopped.
Optus Vision is 46.5 percent owned by both Australian telecommunications carrier Optus Communications and Continental CableVision Inc, which has merged with U.S. West.
The balance of Optus Vision is owned by Seven Network Ltd and Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
